Flux itself is one app, but its full capability rests on a small set of external tools:
Node for a source checkout, Quarto (+ TeX) for compiling manuscripts, a Python
environment with **fluxplot** for semantic plots, and the house fonts for faithful
rendering. This page is the complete checklist for a fresh machine.

# Installing Flux itself

## From a packaged release

Grab the artifact for your platform from the GitHub Releases page (`.dmg` for macOS,
`.AppImage`/`.deb` for Linux x64) and install normally. The release matrix qualifies macOS
Apple Silicon and Intel on their respective native runners. Windows code portability checks
do not imply that a Windows installer is published.

**macOS note:** unsigned builds are ad-hoc signed so they run, but a *downloaded* app is
Gatekeeper-quarantined — the first launch needs right-click → Open (or
`xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine /Applications/Flux.app`). A locally-built app (below) has
no such friction.

## From source

```bash
git clone https://github.com/fluxsci/flux ~/flux
cd ~/flux
npm ci                     # needs Node ≥ 22.15 (see below)
npm run dist:mac           # or dist:linux → installers in release/
```

`~/flux` is only a convention — clone anywhere you like; Flux resolves its own location at
runtime. What *does* matter is that the checkout stays put afterwards: first run bakes its
location into the stable agent launcher and the stock context docs. Run setup again
after moving the installation. (Contrast
[fluxplot](#uv-python-fluxplot-the-keystone) below, where the path is a genuine requirement.)

For development instead of packaging: `npm run electron:dev` (Vite dev server + Electron,
hot reload). A source checkout is also currently required for
[**Lighttable**](lighttable.qmd), the image-set triage companion — it isn't bundled into
packaged builds.

# The critical companions

## Node.js ≥ 22.15

A source checkout needs Node 22.15 or newer. The stable launcher pins the runtime
for that installation; packaged Flux uses its bundled Electron runtime for the CLI
and MCP server. For source work, install Node through your platform's usual channel
(nvm, Homebrew, apt) and check:

```bash
node --version    # v22.15+
```

## Quarto + TinyTeX

Quarto compiles manuscripts to HTML/DOCX/PDF (it bundles its own pandoc — no separate
install). **PDF output additionally needs a TeX distribution**; TinyTeX via Quarto is the
easy path:

```bash
# install quarto from quarto.org (or brew install --cask quarto / apt) — equivalent
quarto install tinytex
quarto check               # verify both halves
```

Without TinyTeX, `flux compile --to pdf` fails while `--to html|docx` still work.

**TinyTeX is not added to your PATH.** `quarto install tinytex` installs into
`~/Library/TinyTeX` (macOS) or `~/.TinyTeX` (Linux) and leaves your PATH alone. Flux and
Quarto don't care — they locate TinyTeX internally, so PDF export works either way. But
`tlmgr` and `kpsewhich` below are TeX's own commands, so without this they fail with
*command not found* even on a perfectly good install:

```bash
# macOS — add to ~/.zshrc to make it permanent
export PATH="$HOME/Library/TinyTeX/bin/universal-darwin:$PATH"
# Linux — add to ~/.bashrc
export PATH="$HOME/.TinyTeX/bin/x86_64-linux:$PATH"
```

### Extras for journal-styled PDF

Exporting with a journal style (Nature, say) asks LaTeX for things a minimal
install may not have: **line numbers**, **double spacing**, a **Times-compatible
font**, and a way to place Flux's SVG figures in a PDF. How you add them depends
on how TeX got onto the machine:

| TeX install | Command | Needs admin? |
|---|---|---|
| TinyTeX (`quarto install tinytex` — recommended, all platforms) | `tlmgr install lineno setspace` | No — TinyTeX lives in your home directory |
| MacTeX | `sudo tlmgr install lineno setspace` | Yes |
| Linux distro TeX Live (apt) | `sudo apt install texlive-latex-recommended texlive-humanities texlive-luatex texlive-fonts-recommended` | Yes — Debian and Ubuntu disable `tlmgr` package installs |

Figures also need **`rsvg-convert`** (`librsvg2-bin` on Debian and Ubuntu,
`librsvg` on Homebrew and Arch): Flux renders figures as SVG, and LaTeX cannot
place those directly.

Check what you have (both `tlmgr` and `kpsewhich` need TinyTeX on your PATH — see above):

```bash
kpsewhich lineno.sty setspace.sty   # both should print a path
rsvg-convert --version              # needed for figures in PDF
```

None of this affects **Word**, which is what Nature prefers for submission
anyway — a journal-styled `.docx` needs no TeX at all. When an export does hit a
missing piece, Flux names the package to install instead of showing you the raw
LaTeX log.

## uv + Python + fluxplot (the keystone)

[uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/) is the recommended Python project/environment manager —
Flux's agent conventions assume it (agents set up a uv project per analysis, with
fluxplot as a dependency).

```bash
curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh | sh          # install uv
git clone https://github.com/fluxsci/fluxplot ~/fluxplot   # fluxplot lives HERE
```

**fluxplot must be cloned to `~/fluxplot`** — that's the conventional location agents
look for (and add as a dependency) when setting up analysis projects. In any analysis
project:

```bash
uv init
uv add --editable ~/fluxplot
uv add cmasher             # the continuous-colormap extra fluxplot[style] uses
```

Why it's the keystone: fluxplot emits *semantic* SVGs — every series, point, and axis
label carries a stable id. That is what makes Flux figures restylable per-part,
regenerable without losing hand-tuning, and morphable in slides. Without it, plots
import as opaque images.

## Fonts

Fluxplot saves plot text as *real text*, and Flux rasterizes figures with the fonts
installed on the machine. The house style's stacks lead with **Arial / Helvetica**
(sans) and **Georgia / Times New Roman / Latin Modern** (serif), falling back to DejaVu.

- **macOS**: Arial, Helvetica, Georgia, Times New Roman are system fonts — you're
  covered. (DejaVu is *not* present; avoid relying on it in cross-machine workflows.)
- **Linux**: install the MS core fonts (`ttf-mscorefonts-installer` on Debian/Ubuntu) or
  accept the DejaVu look. Latin Modern comes with TeX (`fonts-lmodern`).
- **Rule of thumb**: keep the *generating* machine and the *rendering* machine font-
  consistent — matplotlib embeds whichever family it actually picked, and the renderer
  substitutes anything missing, which shifts text metrics subtly.

# First run

Launching Flux (or a CLI command) initializes `~/FluxConfig`: your **UserContext**,
the stock **FluxContext** manual, and the **FluxLib** reference library. Your personal
context is seeded once; the stock manual is refreshed with this installation's paths.

Flux creates stable `flux` and `flux-connect` launchers in `~/.local/share/flux/bin`
(Linux/macOS), or `%LOCALAPPDATA%\flux\bin` (Windows). Add that folder to PATH or
use its full path. When `~/.local/bin` exists, Flux also adds convenience shims there;
`flux connect setup --create-local-bin` can create them. Your own unmarked files are
preserved. Flux prints PATH guidance and never changes shell startup files for you.

The launcher stays with its owning installation across starts from other checkouts.
Use **AI status → Use this Flux for agents**, or setup's `--use-this-install`, to
choose another. AppImage launchers use the persistent AppImage file. On macOS, move
Flux into `/Applications` before setup to avoid a temporary App Translocation path.

1. Fill out `~/FluxConfig/Context/UserContext/WHO-AM-I.md`.
2. Adjust `UserContext/RULES.md` and add reusable procedures under `UserContext/Skills/`.
3. Moving machines? Copy your UserContext (including Skills), FluxLib and global
   `plot_library/`. FluxContext is regenerated; run agent setup on the new machine.

See [Your context and your project's](agents/context.qmd) before opening older projects
that need migration.

# Connect an AI agent

Install and sign in to Claude Code or Codex in its own app or terminal. Open **AI** in
the titlebar, or **Ctrl+K → AI status**, then choose **Connect** on its card. The Home
screen's **Connect an AI agent** card opens the same monitor. Review replacements if
shown, then restart open agent sessions. In Codex, review newly installed hooks in
**/hooks**. This registers tools and skills; it does not start a project session.

From a terminal the equivalent is `flux connect setup --dry-run`, then `flux connect
setup`, followed by `flux connect doctor`. Copy the panel's `/flux-connect <project>`
or `$flux-connect <project>` command into your agent to connect a session. See
[Working with AI agents](agents/connect.qmd) for the reading plan, receipt and status rows.

# Verify the setup

```bash
node --version                            # ≥ 22.15
quarto check                              # quarto + tinytex
uv --version
uv run python -c "import fluxplot"        # inside an analysis project
flux config                              # prints machine paths + build info
flux connect doctor                      # checks the Flux AI Bundle
```

# Troubleshooting

| Symptom | Cause → fix |
|---|---|
| `compile --to pdf` fails; html works | No TeX → `quarto install tinytex` |
| Journal PDF fails with `File 'lineno.sty' not found` (or `setspace.sty`) | Minimal TeX install → the journal-PDF table above |
| Journal PDF fails mentioning `rsvg-convert` | SVG figures cannot be placed → install `librsvg2-bin` / `librsvg` |
| Journal PDF fails with `luaotfload` or `not loadable: Metric` | lualatex present but its fonts are not → `texlive-luatex` + `texlive-fonts-recommended`, or use TinyTeX |
| Plots import as flat images; `restyle` finds no parts | Plot not saved via `fp.save` (or fluxplot missing) → check `flux validate-plot` |
| Figure PNGs render with wrong/shifted text | Missing fonts on this machine → install the stacks above; keep machines consistent |
| `flux: command not found` | Launcher directory not on `PATH` → use the full path above, or setup with `--create-local-bin` and add `~/.local/bin` to PATH |
| `flux` CLI verb missing that the docs mention | Stale bundle → `npm run build:cli` in the repo; `flux version` shows the build |
| Agent has no Flux tools or skill | Run `flux connect doctor`, use **AI status → Repair**, then restart the agent session |
| Nothing live-reloads in the open app | Watcher failed to start (a toast said so at open) → reopen the project |
| Flux "won't start" — no window, no error | A windowless earlier instance is holding the single-instance lock (the launch now says so in the terminal) → `pgrep -af electron` to find it, then `kill <pid>` (plain SIGTERM — it saves unsaved work on the way out; keep `kill -9` as the last resort) |
